newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Ashanti Q2 down, but upbeat on outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ashanti Q2 down, but upbeat on outlook.

text.p: Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd on Tuesday reported a sharp fall in second-quarter profits, but said it was on track to meet its 1997 production and cost targets.
Output increases and further cost reductions should also help results next year, chief financial officer Mark Keatley told Reuters.
But a lower gold price and an exceptional charge for redundancy costs hit 1997 second-quarter earnings, which fell to $7.7 million from $13.4 million a year ago.

In a move to trim its cost base Ashanti, which is West Africa's largest gold miner, cut the number of jobs at its main Obuasi gold mine by 800 to just below 10,000. This resulted in an exceptional charge of $2.5 million.
Ashanti realised a gold price of $450 per ounce in the second quarter compared with $465 a year ago.

But an active hedging policy cushioned the impact of far lower gold prices on depressed world spot market. Ashanti said it has over five million ounces hedged at a price of over $420 per ounce. Of total 1998 production, 80 percent is hedged at $428 per ounce, Keatley said.
"We are quite well protected against the gold price and I think the analysts are therefore expecting a slight (earnings) increase next year which is broadly correct," he told Reuters.

"Twenty percent of our production is still exposed to the gold price. So one cannot predict that, but we would expect there would be some increase (in 1998 earnings) depending on the gold price," Keatley said.

Market forecasts for full 1997 earnings, meanwhile, vary between $40 and $50 million, and are in line with the company's own expectations. Commenting on the analysts' range, Keatly said: "It's broadly correct."
He added Obuasi's production is set to increase in the second half of 1997 after just failing to meet first-half targets.

The Obuasi mine produced 417,000 ounces in the first six months of the year against an objective of 420,000. Output was restricted by power supply disruptions and extraordinary rainfall, Keatley said.
But the gradual build-up of underground production and extraction of gold from an old part of the mine will boost overall output in the second half, he added.
Ashanti is confident that the 1997 objective to produce 1.1 million ounces at $265 per ounce will be met.

Looking further ahead, Keatley said 1998 profits will be underpinned by further cost reduction at Obuasi. The start-up in the second half of 1998 of the new Bibiani and Siguiri mines will also help, Keatley said.
Bibiani and Siguiri are Ashanti's main exploration projects in respectively Ghana and Guinea.
Ashanti left its interim dividend unchanged at $0.125 per share.
